# Dev Push Notification

Easiest way to add push notifications to your React web app.

## Installation

1. Install the library along with command:

```bash
npm install dev-push-notification
```

2. Copy the service worker file to your project’s public folder:
   - Download from: <a href="https://dev-push-notification.vercel.app/dpn-sw.js" download="dpn-sw.js">dpn-sw.js</a>
   - Place it in your project at: `public/dpn-sw.js`

```bash
/public/dpn-sw.js
```

> ⚠️ **This step is required:**  
> The file must be named `dpn-sw.js` and placed in the `public` folder for push notifications to work in production.

## 🔑 API Key

> ⚠️ You must have an API key to use this package.
>
> 👉 [Get API Key](https://dev-push-notification.vercel.app/api-section)

## Usage

Here’s a simple example using React:

```javascript
import { useState, useEffect } from "react";
import {
  getToken,
  sendNotification,
  onMessageListener,
  initMessaging,
} from "dev-push-notification";

const App = () => {
  const [token, setToken] = useState(null);
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState("");

  const API_KEY = "YOUR_API_KEY_HERE";

  // Listen for push notifications (important: place this in App.jsx)
  useEffect(() => {
    initMessaging(API_KEY);
    const unsubscribe = onMessageListener((payload) => {
      console.log("Notification received:", payload);
      if (Notification.permission === "granted" && payload.notification) {
        const { title, body, image } = payload.notification;
        new Notification(title, { body, icon: image });
      }
    }, API_KEY);

    return () => unsubscribe();
  }, []);

  // Get device token (store it in your DB if needed)
  const handleGetToken = async () => {
    try {
      setLoading("getToken");
      const token = await getToken(API_KEY);
      setToken(token);
      console.log("Device token:", token);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error("Failed to get token:", err);
    } finally {
      setLoading("");
    }
  };

  // Send a push notification
  const handleSendNotification = async () => {
    try {
      setLoading("sendNotification");
      const res = await sendNotification({
        apiKey: API_KEY,
        title: "Hello",
        body: "This is a test push notification",
        icon: "https://example.com/icon.png",
        fcmTokens: [token], // here you can pass multiple tokens at a time it's array of sting
      });
      console.log("Notification sent response:", res);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error("Failed to send notification:", err);
    } finally {
      setLoading("");
    }
  };

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={handleGetToken}>
        {loading === "getToken" ? "Generating..." : "Get Token"}
      </button>

      <button onClick={handleSendNotification} disabled={!token}>
        {loading === "sendNotification" ? "Sending..." : "Send Notification"}
      </button>
    </div>
  );
};

export default App;
```

## Important Notes

1. **Service Worker is required:**  
   Make sure `/public/dpn-sw.js` exists in your project.

2. **HTTPS required in production:**  
   Push notifications only work on HTTPS or localhost.

3. **Notification permissions:**  
   Users must allow notifications in their browser.
